audit.whatIsWrong: The page invented an ability and an effect: content whys[4] and spikes[1] call his level 6 'Rake Reaping's execute', and content mid calls it 'his level 6 execute burst'. Rake is his W, his ultimate is Shadow Assault, and nothing in Talon's kit executes. It also never mentioned Blade's End, which is where most of his damage actually comes from.
audit.why: Riot's text: R 'disperses a ring of blades and becomes Invisible while gaining additional Move Speed. When Talon emerges from Invisibility, the blades converge on his location.' Passive: 'Talon's spells Wound champions... stacking up to 3 times. When Talon attacks a champion with 3 stacks of Wound, they bleed for heavy damage over time.' The blades converge where HE reappears, so leaving that point is the answer, and the third Wound stack plus an auto is the real kill trigger.
audit.corrected: whys[4], spikes[1] and content mid rewritten around Shadow Assault's real behaviour and its 100-second rank-1 cooldown; report[5].t, dontsFull[0].d, dontsFull[2].d and content early now carry the Blade's End three-stack bleed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full layer gave Levels 1 through 5 to Talon (phases[0..3].side = 'Talon') and the rest to 'Skill', while content win[0..6] and the packet levelChart both read Aurora on all seven rows. Worse, the four Talon-side rows carried whys that describe Aurora winning them.
audit.why: phases[N].side and win[N] are the same row. Packet and content agree on Aurora x7, the full-layer whys already argued Aurora, and 50.54% over 1391 games fits a lane Aurora edges by respecting one engage.
audit.corrected: All seven sides set to Aurora, the four 7/10 ratings brought down to 5/10 to match the page's own convention, and every affected why rewritten in the same proposal around Talon's real numbers (Q 8s and a 575 leap, Rake 9s, Blade's End at three stacks, Shadow Assault 100s).

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text credited Aurora's escape to 'Twin Drift', which is not an ability in either kit, and tied Talon's spike to a level 6 execute that does not exist.
audit.why: Aurora's dash is Across the Veil (22s at rank 1), named by the full layer itself. Talon's real spikes are level 3 (Rake plus the vault-into-leap combo), level 6 Shadow Assault, and a completed lethality item.
audit.corrected: spikes[0].text, whys[0], content early and wants.you[0] now name Across the Veil, Assassin's Path and Noxian Diplomacy's 575 leap; spikes[1] rebuilt on Shadow Assault.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit, and dosFull[2].d invented a 'fifteen-second invitation' for Rake.
audit.why: Rake is 9/8.5/8/7.5/7 — nine seconds at rank 1. The genuinely important cooldown on this champion is not on an ability at all: Assassin's Path costs almost nothing, but it puts the terrain he vaulted on a long cooldown, so the wall he entered through is not available as his exit.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now carries Rake 9s, Noxian Diplomacy 8s and 575 range, and the terrain-cooldown rule. dosFull[2].d says 9-second window.

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeGood/tradeBad and the two bullets that reused them verbatim (dosFull[1].d, dontsFull[2].d) were generic and said nothing about Talon.
audit.why: The specific trade fact is that Noxian Diplomacy leaps only from 575 while Aurora pokes from 900, and that standing still for the Q recast is what feeds him the third Wound stack.
audit.corrected: Both trade strings, the trading breakdown, report[3].t and the two bled bullets rewritten around those numbers, each matched to its own title.

audit.why: 50.54% over 1391 games; the TRICKY label and 7/10 difficulty are defensible for a lane that is even only if the vault is respected.

notes: 'Rake Reaping' does not exist — Rake is Talon's W and his ultimate is Shadow Assault. The bigger error is that the page told the reader Talon has an execute at 6; he has none, so a player was being taught to fear a threshold that does not exist and to disengage at the wrong moment. Packet suspectName 'Your Between Worlds' is a false positive. The kit lists Assassin's Path cd as 0 and says the terrain it uses goes on a long cooldown, but gives no number for that terrain cooldown, so I described the behaviour without asserting a duration. Talon's W carries a 'knockup' derived flag, but Riot's description of Rake mentions only damage and a slow on the return — per the brief's rule I trusted the description and asserted no displacement anywhere. Content whys[5]/spikes[2] name Youmuu's/Duskblade for Talon, which is plausible but unsourced from the kits; left alone.
